rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING AN ADDITIONAL GROUND FOR CANCELLING THE CERTIFICATE OF CANDIDACY OF A CANDIDATE AND MAKING THE ACTS OF A NUISANCE CANDIDATE AN ELECTION OFFENSE, AMENDING SECTIONS 69, 261 (CC) AND 264 OF BATAS PAMBANSA BLG. 881, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “OMNIBUS ELECTION CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES”
rows.title_short: Providing An Additional Ground For Cancelling The Certificate Of Candidacy Of A Candidate And Making The Acts Of A Nuisance Candidate An Election Offense, Amending Sections 69, 261 ( C C ) And 264 Of Batas Pambansa Blg. 881, As Amended, Otherwise Known As The “ Omnibus Election Code Of The Philippines ”
rows.abstract:
States that the Commission on Elections may refuse to give due course to or cancel a certificate of candidacy if the intention of the candidate is to obtain money, profit, or any other consideration.
Adds the following prohibited acts on candidacy and campaign: a.) to put the election process in mockery or dispute; b.) to maliciously or deliberately cause confusion among the voters by similarity of the names of the registered candidates; c.) to obtain money, profit, or any other consideration; or d.) by any other circumstances or acts which clearly demonstrate that the candidate has no bona fide intention to run for the office for which the certificate of candidacy has been filed and thus prevent a faithful determination of the true will of electorate. 
Prescribes a fine of Five Hundred Thousand Pesos (Php500, 000.00) for any person guilty of the election offense enumerated in this Act.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2025-02-03, transmitted to the Senate on 2025-02-04 and received by the Senate on 2025-02-04

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE RIGHTS OF INFORMAL AMBULANT VENDORS
rows.title_short: Magna Carta For Informal Ambulant Vendors
rows.abstract:
Aims to recognize the significant contribution of informal ambulant vendors to the economy, safeguard their livelihoods, and promote their welfare. 
Requires all informal ambulant vendors to register with the city, municipality, or barangay where they are vending or intend to vend within the territorial jurisdiction of such city, municipality or barangay.
Provides the rights of informal ambulant vendors such as 1.) Right to renewal of registration as informal ambulant vendors for such designated vending place, subject to said person´s continued qualifications as an informal ambulant vendor; 2.) Right to security of tenure in the designated vending place as assigned by the concerned LGU; c.) Right to be recognized in other LGUs upon securing a prior certificate from the other LGU; and d.) Right to social protection and safety nets, labor markets programs, and social welfare interventions such as social security, health care, and insurance.
Mandates the City or Municipal Mayor to establish a Local Inter-Agency Council through an appropriate local ordinance which shall be responsible for coordinating efforts to ensure the security and protection of registered informal ambulant vendors.
Provides that registered informal ambulant vendors shall not be arbitrarily deprived of their vending sites nor their stall demolished without due process of law.
Requires all registered informal ambulant vendors to comply with basic health and safety standards to be established by the concerned LGU in coordination with the Local Inter-Agency Council in accordance with RA 11058.

rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A NATIONAL POLICY FRAMEWORK FOR THE DEVELOPMENT, UTILIZATION, AND COMMERCIALIZATION OF ENERGY STORAGE SYSTEMS
rows.title_short: Energy Storage Systems Act
rows.abstract:
Aims to improve the reliability and flexibility of the Grid to accommodate the growing demand for sustainable renewable energy back up or ancillary sources of electricity such as solar and wind, as part of the country´s just transition plans; establish the necessary fiscal or non-fiscal mechanisms to encourage the development, utilization, and commercialization of energy storage systems in both Grid and off-Grid areas in the country; and help secure additional sources of power supply that shall meet the country´s growing demand.
Enumerates the powers and responsibilities of different government agencies for the implementation and enforcement of this Act.
Provides incentives for Integrated Renewable Energy (RE) Plant and Energy Storage System (ESS) such as: a.) The ESS developer may avail of the incentives Under Chapter VII of RA 9513 for its Integrated RE Plant and ESS; b.) Integrated RE Plants and ESS that use a combination of Conventional Plant/s and an ESS, the incentives shall be granted in proportion to and to the extent of the RE component utilized; and c.) the Integrated RE Plant and ESS, as applicable, shall have preferential dispatch, but it can choose to be registered as a schedule generating unit.

rows.title_full: AN ACT ENHANCING ANIMAL INDUSTRY DEVELOPMENT AND COMPETITIVENESS,   STRENGTHENING THE BUREAU OF ANIMAL INDUSTRY, AND CREATING FOR THE PURPOSE AN ANIMAL COMPETITIVENESS ENHANCEMENT FUND
rows.title_short: Animal Industry Development And Competitiveness Act
rows.abstract:
Aims to advance the animal industry through robust regulatory and development institutions, adequate resources for production support especially for small farmers and producers, sound laws and regulation, effective coordination and collaboration with stakeholders, and credible standards and measures for safety and quality of animal products. 
Expands and reclassifies the Bureau of Animal Industry (BAI) into a line agency attached to the Department of Agriculture (DA), with regional and provincial offices whose creation is hereby authorized.
Creates the Animal Competitiveness Enhancement Fund (AnCEF) with an annual appropriation of Twenty billion pesos (P20,000,000,000.00) following the effectivity of this act and ten (10) years thereafter.
Establishes the Livestock Registry System (LRS) which shall have the master list of eligible beneficiaries of the AnCEF in consultation with farmers´ cooperatives and organization and local government units (LGUs).
Provides the BAI, in consultation with the LGUs and stakeholders, the power to issue administrative orders and regulations for the conservation, preservation, management and sustainable development of the animal industry.  
Provides prohibitions and penalties for the violations of this Act.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A COMPREHENSIVE FISCAL AUTONOMY FOR THE JUDICIARY, CREATING FOR THE PURPOSE THE JUDICIARY TRUST FUND
rows.title_short: Judiciary Fiscal Autonomy Act
rows.abstract:
Seeks to affirm and strengthen the constitutional mandate and powers of the Judiciary as a co-equal branch of government.
Establishes the Judiciary Trust Fund for the use and operation of the Judiciary particularly to grant or augment allowances and other benefits to members and personnel of the Judiciary and to finance the acquisition, maintenance, and repair of office equipment and facilities.
Grants the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court to administer and allocate the Judiciary Trust Fund and to approve and authorize disbursements and expenditures of the same in accordance with the guidelines set in this Act and its implementing rules and regulations.
Authorizes the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court to realign the budget from one expense account to another, except the Capital Outlays, or from one functional unit or category to another, without the need for the approval of the Department of Budget and Management (DBM).
Authorizes the Supreme Court to determine the number and positions of court personnel necessary for the effective functioning of the Judiciary, within the limits of approved appropriations and guided by constitutional and legislative policies on hiring and compensation.
Incorporates the budget proposal prepared by the Supreme Court in the National Expenditure Program (NEP) without any revision.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A COMPREHENSIVE AND RESPONSIVE CIVIL REGISTRATION AND VITAL STATISTICS SYSTEM
rows.title_short: Philippine Civil Registry Act
rows.abstract:
Seeks to establish a more efficient and inclusive standardized and modernized civil registration system that shall be used as the evidence base for social, economic, and health policy.
Defines the duties and powers of the Civil Registrar General and the City/Municipal Civil Registrar.
Mandates the local civil registrar to maintain, keep, and preserve in a secured place the Books of registry where the acts, events, judicial decrees or orders concerning the civil status of persons are properly entered.
Provides for a free registration of vital civil registry events including late registrations.
Provides for mandatory continuing education and training program for Civil Registrars, Consul Generals, District Recorders, Circuit Registrars and their staff to ensure the efficient delivery of civil registration services.
Establishes the Indigenous Peoples Civil Registration System (IPCRS) that is sensitive and appropriate to the unique cultural practices and identification systems of ICCs/IPs.
Establishes the Barangay Civil Registration System (BCRS) where elected and appointed barangay officials shall be mandated to assist in the facilitation of civil registration within the area of jurisdiction.
Mandates the digitalization of civil registration processes and the national register, local registers and other records.

rows.title_short: People Empowerment Act
rows.abstract:
Seeks to empower the people by providing them greater access and participation to governance through Civil Society Organizations (CSO).
Mandates CSOs to have actively operated for at least one (1) year in the city or municipality where majority of its members reside, and must apply for accreditation with the local sanggunian upon submission of prescribed requirements.
Provides for a creation of People´s Council, composed of accredited CSOs, in each local government unit (LGU) wherein members may participate in the conceptualization, implementation and evaluation of government activities, among others.
Creates a Committee for the Accreditation of CSOs in all provincial, city and municipal sanggunians wherein two (2) representatives shall come from the People´s Council.
Creates a Provincial People´s Council (PPC) recognized by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan and shall be composed of all representatives from the municipal and city People´s Councils within a province´s jurisdiction wherein a representative elected within their ranks shall sit as a member of the Sanggunian Panlalawigan and shall exercise the duties and powers of a Provincial Board member.
Mandates barangays to provide information boards and suggestion boxes to be strategically situated in public places accessible to the people.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE MAGNA CARTA OF CHILDREN
rows.title_short: The Magna Carta Of Children
rows.abstract:
Seeks to codify existing legislation and harmonize it with the provisions of United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child (UNCRC) to protect the rights of children.
Embodies the four basic principles of the UNRC: the children´s right to non-discrimination, the best interest of children, their right to life and development, and their right to participation in all matters that affect them.
Mandates all government offices, including local government units to adopt a comprehensive and integrated strategy through the development and implementation of laws, policies, regulatory instruments, administrative guidelines, and other appropriate measures to implement the provisions of this Act and other related laws and policies and uphold the rights of Filipino children and create an environment that would steer their growth and well-being in all aspects of life.

rows.title_short: Strengthening The Mechanism For Land Use Development And Infrastructure Planning And Budgeting For State Universities And Colleges ( S U Cs ), Amending For The Purpose Republic Act No. 11396, Otherwise Known As The `` S U Cs Land Use Development And Infrastructure Plan ( L U D I P ) Act
rows.abstract:
Seeks to improve the manner by which state universities and colleges (SUCs) formulate their respective land use development and infrastructure plans (LUDIPs) which covers a five-year period and shall contain priority infrastructure projects.
Provides that the preparation and implementation of the LUDIP shall be a requirement for the approval of infrastructure projects in SUCs.
Mandates the CHED to include the LUDIP of each SUC in a five-(5)-year comprehensive LUDIP for all compliant SUCs within one (1) year from the receipt thereof and submit it to Congress and other government agencies concerned to guide the allocation of funds for the land use and infrastructure projects of the SUCs on an annual basis.
Mandates all government department, agencies, offices, and instrumentalities to extend all possible assistance and cooperation to all SUCs in the preparation of their LUDIP.

rows.abstract:

Provides for the following: 1.) additional qualifications and requirements for ERC Commissioners to ensure board diversity; 2.) prohibitions and disqualifications for ERC Commissioners and their relatives to prevent conflict of interest; 3.) the separation of the Chairperson and CEO functions to assure balance of power; 4.) defined duties and responsibilities of the Chairperson, the Commission, and the Executive Director to increase individual and board accountability; 5.) open meetings during deliberations of the Commission to guarantee public transparency; 6.) access to information to enhance knowledge and education on regulatory matters affecting public welfare; and 7.) liabilities for violation of among, among others, open meeting and access to information provisions.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROMOTING INVESTMENTS IN LOW CARBON ECONOMY, ESTABLISHING FOR THIS PURPOSE A CARBON EMISSION PRICING FRAMEWORK AND IMPLEMENTATION MECHANISM TO ACHIEVE LOW CARBON AND CLIMATE-RESILIENT ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT
rows.title_short: Low Carbon Economy Investment Act
rows.abstract:
Aims to achieve the country´s national climate targets by instituting a comprehensive carbon emission pricing framework and implementing mechanisms that drive greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions reduction, enhance climate resilience, and foster sustainable economic growth.
Institutionalizes the Philippine Greenhouse Gas Inventory System (PGHGIS) designed to enable Philippines to transition towards a climate-resilient pathway, promoting the avoidance, reduction, and removal of emissions for sustainable development. 
Mandates the Climate Change Commission (CCC) to institutionalize the National Integrated Climate Change Database and Information Exchange System (NICCDIES) as the primary platform for climate change and resilience information.
Establishes the Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) which shall serve as the Philippines´ long-term roadmap for GHG mitigation and climate resilience, outlining the country´s commitments to reducing emissions and adapting to climate impacts.
Establishes a comprehensive Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification (MRV) system to track mitigation outcomes and the accomplishments of the NDC.
Mandates all covered enterprises to prepare a decarbonization plan aligned with the objectives to limit global temperature rise to below two degrees Celsius (2Â°C) above pre-industrial levels, with the goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2050.
Provides the methodology for pricing carbon emissions based on mitigation cost component and preventive resilience cost component.
Requires all covered enterprises to submit an Annual Compliance Report to the DENR containing emissions baseline and reduction progress, reduction activities and outcomes, emissions allowance and excess emissions, allocation of decarbonization funds, and future plans.

rows.title_short: P200 Across-the- Board Daily Wage Increase Act
rows.abstract:
Seeks to increase the daily rate of all minimum wage workers in the private sector, regardless of employment status, including those in contractual and sub-contractual arrangements, whether agricultural or nonagricultural by Two hundred pesos (P200.00) per day.
Provides incentives to small enterprises to assist in their compliance with the wage increase.
Exempts the Barangay Micro Business Enterprises (BMBEs) from the coverage of the Minimum Wage Law as provided by RA 9178.
Allows the following establishments to apply exemption from the compliance with the minimum wage increase: a.) retail or service establishments regularly employing not more than ten (10) workers; and b.) establishments adversely affected by natural calamities or human-induced disasters.
Provides penalties to any person, corporation, trust, firm, partnership, association, or entity violating any provision of this Act.

rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE PHILIPPINE MERCHANT MARINE ACADEMY BY RENAMING IT AS THE PHILIPPINE NATIONAL MARITIME ACADEMY, EXPANDING ITS MANDATE, CURRICULAR OFFERINGS, AND THE COMPOSITION OF THE GOVERNING BOARD, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.title_short: Philippine National Maritime Academy Charter
rows.abstract:
Seeks to rename the Philippine Merchant Marine Academy (PMMA) to Philippine National Marine Academy (PNMA) that shall provide holistic education and training for human resource development of maritime students, professionals, and leaders in support of maritime industry development, maritime law enforcement, and national security.
Provides for the responsibilities, powers and functions of the PNMA.
Mandates graduate of the merchant marine courses of the PNMA to serve in the government for an accumulated duration of at least four (4) years.
Ensures the proper distribution of the cadets availing the quality education and opportunities in the PNMA by establishing a system by which every Congressional District is given the opportunity to send cadets governed by the principle of merit and fitness.
Provides that the campuses in any part of the country may be established, subject to the approval of the Board of Trustees.

rows.title_full: AN ACT MAINSTREAMING THE USE OF BAMBOO AS A SUSTAINABLE MATERIAL FOR THE BUILT ENVIRONMENT
rows.title_short: Bamboo For A Sustainable Built Environment Act
rows.abstract:
Seeks to establish a comprehensive regulatory framework for the integration of bamboo as a sustainable material for the built environment in the Philippines.
Tasks relevant agencies and stakeholders with developing the Bamboo Architectural Code (BAC) and Bamboo Structural Code (BSC) which shall include guidelines and standards for the sustainable use of bamboo, aesthetics, safety, environmental impact, and cultural consideration.
Encourages public awareness campaigns, educational programs, and incentives for bamboo cultivation.
Integrates bamboo-related education into higher education curricula and continuing education for architects, interior designers, and engineers.

rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING THE ASSISTANCE TO INDIVIDUALS IN CRISIS SITUATIONS PROGRAM OF THE DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL WELFARE AND DEVELOPMENT, PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR THE VIOLATION OF CERTAIN UNLAWFUL ACTS, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.title_short: Assistance To Individuals In Crisis Situations ( A I C S )   Act
rows.abstract:
Seeks to institutionalize a permanent national program that is financially and administratively capable of responding to the needs of Filipinos when dealing with an extreme circumstance.
Provides each qualified beneficiary with financial, medical, transportation, food, material, and other assistance including disability support services, psychosocial support or intervention for dysfunctional families and their children who need trauma case and management, and legal consultation, based on the assessment of the social workers of the DSWD.
Establishes an Integrated Program Delivery System for real-time data sharing between the DSWD and the LGUs in order to identify the assistance given to the Program´s eligible beneficiary for purposes of assistance augmentation and to prevent possible abuse of the assistance given to those in crisis situations.
Establishes the Crisis Intervention Office (ICO) at the Central Office, Crisis Intervention Divisions at the field offices, and Crisis Intervention Units at the Social Welfare and Development satellite offices of the DSWD that shall monitor and evaluate the implementation of AICS Program and prepare the monitoring and evaluation report for submission to the Secretary of the DSWD.
 Provides unlawful acts and corresponding penalties to prevent abuse of the AICS program.

rows.title_short: Expanding The Coverage Of The Senior Citizens Privileges And Benefits, Further Amending Republic Act No. 7432, As Amended, Entitled “ An Act To Maximize The Contribution Of Senior Citizens To Nation Building, Grant Benefits, And Special Privileges And For Other Purposes ”
rows.abstract:
Amends Sec. 2 of RA 7432, as amended, by defining medicines and food supplements.
Includes online sales on the twenty percent (20%) discount on medicines, professional fees of attending physicians, licensed professional health workers, medical and dental services, dental services, diagnostic and  laboratory fees, medical facilities, outpatient clinics, and home care services  including payments made through health maintenance organizations or insurance companies.
Grants twenty percent (20%) discount in Transport Network Vehicle Services (TNVS), payment of toll fees in skyways, and expressways, and golf and country clubs.
Grants fifteen percent (15%) discount on the monthly utilization of water and electricity supplied by public utilities which monthly consumption does not exceed two hundred kilowatt hours (200 kWh) of electricity and fifty cubic meters (50 m3) of water, provided that the billing statement is under the name of the senior citizen.
Grants eight and a half percent (8.5%) special discounts on the purchase of basic necessities and prime commodities provided that the total amount of purchase shall not exceed five thousand pesos (Php5,000.00) per calendar week without carry-over of the unused amount.
Grants twenty-five thousand pesos (Php25,000.00) death benefit assistance to the nearest surviving relative of a deceased senior citizen.
Exempts senior citizen from the Unified Vehicular Volume Reduction Program and parking fee.
Grants twenty percent (20%) discount on traffic fines.
